Moot question is whether an acquittal order can be challenged under
Section 372 Cr.P.C. Various High Courts have taken different views and are at variance on this issue. along with definition of 'injury' under Section
44 IPC and Section 22 IPC, it held that non-encashment of the cheque causes 'injury' to the person
in whose favour cheque has been issued. whether to prefer appeal under Section 372 or 378(4) Cr.P.C. But once it is a case instituted on a
complaint and an order of acquittal is passed, whether the offence is bailable or
non-bailable, cognizable or non-cognizable, the complainant can file an application
under Section 378 (4) for special leave to appeal against it in the High Court. 4225,
Full Bench of Gujarat High Court answering the reference on question number (3) 'If the victim
prefers an appeal before this Court, challenging the acquittal, invoking his right under proviso to
section 372 of Cr.P.C., whether that appellant is required to first seek leave of the Court, as is
required in case of appeal being preferred by the State?', held :- 'If the victim also happens to be the
complainant and the appeal is against acquittal, he is required to take leave as provided in Section
378 of the Criminal Procedure Code but if he is not the complainant, he is not required to apply for
or obtain any leave. For the appeal against inadequacy of compensation or punishment on a lesser
offence, no leave is necessary at the instance of a victim, whether he is the complainant or not.'

against an acquittal order in a complaint case, appeal would lie under Section 372 Cr.P.C. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties on this limited legal question and have examined
372 Cr.P.C. incorporating a right of appeal to the victims and also introducing definition of 'victim',
as per Section 2(wa) of Cr.P.C., the appellant being the complainant-cum-victim was entitled to
prefer appeals against orders of acquittal under Section 138 N.I. State of West Bengal', CRR No.2816/2012 and CRAN
No.3690/2012, decided on 12.03.2013. The appellant therein
had sought leave to prefer appeal under Section 378 (4) Cr.P.C. Mangalabai Ashokbhai
Patel and The State of Maharashtra', Crl.Revision Application No.100/2013, decided on 09.12.2013
against acquittal order in the proceedings under Section 138 N.I. State of Rajasthan', S.B.Criminal
Leave to Appeal No.6/2012 decided on 01.05.2012, it was held that the remedy to challenge the
acquittal under Section 138 N.I. State of Rajasthan & anr.', S.B.Criminal Leave to Appeal No.74/2012 decided on 28.02.2013, a
contrary view was taken and it was held that against an order on acquittal under Section 138 N.I. State of Rajasthan & anr.' (supra) was of no
help as the impact of amended proviso to Section 372 Cr.P.C. Needless to say that State / Police has no role
to regulate the proceedings / transactions. Such appeal would be maintainable only if the appellant /
complainant was granted Special Leave to prefer appeal. This was meant for those 'victims' on whose behalf primarily State
used to prosecute the offender(s). In case of acquittal, it was left to the State to challenge the order
in appeal and the victim had no say. It is a separate and independent statutory right and is not dependent either upon or is
subservient to the right of appeal of the State.
